parties:
Sunil Kumar Baidya--------Petitioner (In Writ Petition No. 12536 of 2016)
Vs
Bidhan Biswas and others--------Respondents (In Writ Petition No. 12536 of 2016)
full_judgment:
Syed Refaat Ahmed J: The above writ petitions are being disposed of by a single Judgment as these matters involve common questions of fact and law. The commonality of facts and issues straddling both writ petitions have permitted of an analogous consideration of the two Rules Nisi. It is evident to this Court that the proceedings and deliberations in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 are moot in both cases. The core contention in both the writ petitions is that the Respondent-in-common, Bidhan Biswas is not eligible to be and to remain as Chairman of the Union Parishad in question as because during the election he was effectively a fugitive from law but by concealing that fact and resultantly through a false declaration made he participated in the election and got himself illegally elected. 

 3. Facts, in brief, stated in this application are that the petitioner, Sunil Kumar Baidya is a permanent resident and voter of Kadambari Union of Rajoir Upazilla under Madaripur District and also is the Secretary for Forest and Environment of said Union Awami League. The election of Kadambari Union Parishad ("Union Parishad") was held on 7-5-2016 wherein Bidhan Biswas, Respondent No. 1, being a rebel candidate, took part in the election and was declared elected as Chairman of the said Union Parishad. On 24-5-2016 Gazette was published by the Election Commission and, accordingly, Bidhan Biswas has since been functioning as Chairman of the said Union Parishad. The petitioner filed the instant Writ of Quo Warranto against the Respondent No.1, Bidhan Biswas claiming that the Respondent No. 1 is not eligible to be and to remain as Chairman of the said Union Parishad. The petitioner further claims that at the time of election Bidhan Biswas was a fugitive and concealing the fact concerning his status as a fugitive he submitted nomination paper along with an affidavit with a false declaration that he was not ineligible for the election and got himself illegally elected. The fact of the matter, the petitioner contends, is that being an accused, Bidhan Biswas obtained bail in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 and, thereafter, he did not turn up in Court on the date fixed for hearing. Subsequently, on 22-5-2014 the Court cancelled his bail and declared him a fugitive and issued a warrant of arrest. Against this backdrop, the petitioner brought this Writ Petition and obtained the present Rule Nisi. 

 5. In this application the petitioner, Dinesh Chandra Biswas challenges the dereliction of the Respondents in taking appropriate steps against the Respondent No. 4, Bidhan Biswas under the provisions of sections 34 and 35 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ain, 2009 ("Ain") and also seeks direction upon the Respondent Nos. 1-3 to take appropriate steps for removing Respondent No. 4, Bidhan Biswas following the provisions of the Ain. The core contention is that the Respondent No. 4, Bidhan Biswas is not eligible to be and to remain as Chairman of the Union Parishad for having sworn an affidavit with a false declaration concerning his eligibility under law. The election being held on 7-5-2016, Bidhan Biswas has been elected and functioning as Chairman of the said Parishad. In October 2016 the petitioner came to know that Bidhan Biswas was the sole accused in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 filed under sections 420 and 406 of the Penal Code. As in the other Writ Petition, to here, it is contended that the Respondent No. 4, Bidhan Biswas obtained bail from the Trial Court on 28-11-2013 but, thereafter, he did not turn up in Court ever. Consequently, the Trial Court by an order dated 22-5-2014 cancelled his bail, declared him a fugitive and issued a warrant of arrest. It is submitted that suppressing those facts Bidhan Biswas filed the nomination paper along with the affidavit with a false declaration that he was not ineligible for the election and got himself illegally elected. It is argued, therefore, that the Respondent No. 4, Bidhan Biswas is not eligible to be and to remain as Chairman of the said Union Parishad as per the provision of section 26(2) of the Ain. Since, it is further submitted, according to the law he has been holding or purporting to hold the said office without any lawful authority, Bidhan Biswas is also liable to be removed from the said office for the same reason. It is shown that predicated on these facts on 27-9-2016 the petitioner applied to the concerned authority to take appropriate action and remove Bidhan Biswas from the post of Chairman. 

 6. Mr AF Hasan Ariff, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both writ petitions submits that Bidhan Biswas is a fugitive in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 declared by the competent Court and being a fugitive Bidhan Biswas took part in the election and was elected as Chairman. Thus, Bidhan Biswas is not entitled to hold the post of Chairman anymore. 

 8. By filing Affidavits-in-Opposition Bidhan Biswas has made out his case that he is not the same person who took money from the complainant in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 and that one Pankaj Bhakta by falsely impersonating himself as Bidhan Biswas took money from the complainant. 

 9. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Advocate appearing for Bidhan Biswas in both matters submits that Biswas does not fall to be governed by section 26(2)(taa) as well as sections 31 and 34 of the Ain as because he is not the accused in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 which is pending before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 20, Dhaka. 

 "After hearing the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 1, it transpires that for an effective and fair disposal of this Rule, L/C record of Complaint Case No. 143 of 2011, which is now pending before the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 20, Dhaka is required to be looked into and also presence of the following persons are required namely (i) Sunil Kumar Baidya, son of late Subal Badiya of village Hijalbari, Post Office-Kadambari, Police Station-Rajoir, District-Madaripur, (petitioner) (ii) Bidhan Biswas, son of late Arjun Chandra Biswas, Chairman, Kadambari Union Parishad, Union Parishad Office, Post Office-Kadambari, Police Station-Rajoir, District-Madaripur, (Respondent No. 1) and (iii) Md Mirazur Rahman, son of Moksed Ali, of 23 Professor Ershad Ullah Road, Police Station-Jatrabari, District-Dhaka (Complainant of Complain Case No. 143 of 2011). 

 Accordingly, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka is directed to immediately transmit the LCR of Complaint Case No. 143 of 2011 from the Court No. 20, of the Metropolitan Magistrate Court of Dhaka, and the above named persons are directed to appear before this Court on 16th January, 2017 in-person without any fail. 

 It is against the backdrop of this order, and consequent to it, that one, Pankaj Bhakta has come out of the woodwork in Writ Petition No. 12536 of 2016 by filing an Affidavit-in-Compliance to admit through his learned Advocate, Mr Abdul Jalil of his knowledge about Complaint Case No. 143 of 2011 and informs this Court that, subsequently, it was not prosecuted. He clearly states in Paragraph 2 of the Affidavit-in-Compliance thus: 

 "That I induced (sic) myself as Bidhan Biswas who was the renowned and popular person in this locality as such it was easier for me to take money from the complainant of CR Case No. 143 of 2011 which was pending in the Court below. I also promised with Md Mirazur Rahman to send abroad i.e., Libya but it was not possible for me sending him abroad because of Sanu Gupta who took money to send Libya after some days I could not find him in his as usual address as well as not to contact to his mobile phone subsequently I have arranged all the money and returned to Md Mirazur Rahman who was the complainant of the aforesaid CR case and subsequently was withdrawn on 8-1-2017." 

 Mr Jalil now submits that Bidhan Biswas was indeed not connected to CR Case No. 143 of 2011 and all that has since transpired involving Biswas in the CR Case is a result of bona fide mistake. Mr Jalil impresses upon this Court that his client Mr Bhakta is now remorseful for what he has done and begs unconditional apology of this Court. In his Affidavit-in-Compliance, Mr Bhakta states that he gave the money to one Sanu Gupta, a manpower broker. But Gupta having reneged on his promise to secure Md Mirazur Rahman's employment in Libya, Pankaj Bhakta took it upon himself to refund the money to Md Mirazur Rahman and upon satisfaction of getting his money back Rahman as complainant withdrew the aforesaid case. 

 13. Mr Ariff in replying to Pankaj Bhakta's version of facts denies the veracity of the same. He submits that Pankaj Bhakta has made a false and fabricated story to defraud this Court which cannot be accepted against the statements and evidence on record in the judicial proceeding in CR Case No. 143 of 2011. 

 14. Still staying with the Court order of 9-1-2017 it is noted at this juncture that by filing an Affidavit-in-Compliance, Mr Md Mirazur Rahman, the complainant in CR Case No. 143 of 2011, himself states in attestation of facts as above asserted by Pankaj Bhakta that he handed over an amount of Taka 2,05,000 to Pankaj Bhakta who, however, introduced himself as "Bidhan Biswas". Subsequently, Pankaj Bhakta alias "Bidhan Biswas" having failed to send Mr Rahman to Libya the latter had no alternative but to file CR Case No. 143 of 2011. Mr Rahman now acknowledges that the Respondent Bidhan Biswas as impleaded in these two writ petitions had no involvement in the CR case and admits that Bidhan Biswas and Pankaj Bhakta are indeed two different persons. It is also acknowledged by him that Pankaj Bhakta misrepresented himself as Bidhan Biswas. Mr Rahman further acknowledges that Pankaj Bhakta refunded all his money and he, consequentially, took steps to withdraw the CR Case. He admitted that as per his advice his learned advocate had applied to withdraw the aforesaid CR case which application, however, was not kept in the CR Case record. It is also Mr Rahman's case that he swore an affidavit on 19-10-2016 before the Notary Public affirming and attesting to the facts above. 

 By these statements Mr Md Mirazur Rahman admitted that he had committed a grave but bonafide mistake in filing CR Case No. 143 of 2016 and has begged unconditional apology of this Court. 

 18. It is to note in this context that following this Court's Order dated 9-1-2017, the record of CR Case No. 143 of 2011 was produced before this Court and was duly examined. From a plain reading of the record it appears that Bidhan Biswas was implicated as accused in the said case. However, by an application Bidhan Biswas contended that the accused "Bidhan Biswas" and he are not the one and same person. He claims that his impersonator "Bidhan Biswas" put his signature in the Vokalatnama, bail bond and some other documents in that case. He, the real Bidhan Biswas, also put his signature as deponent of these writ petitions and executed various documents. It is in that context that the signatures on record in CR Case No. 143 of 2011 and the present Writ Petition have been seen by this Court and upon initial comparison are noted to be indeed distinct and not the same. 

 25. Upon a consideration of all the filings before this Court and the case records of CR Case No. 143 of 2011, it is this Court's considered view that the merit of much of the petitioners' cases in both instances have been severely eroded by fact that the credibility and the intention of both the complainant in the CR Case Md Mirazur Rahman and that of Mr Pankaj Bhakta, the self-declared impersonator, are highly suspect. The plethora of affidavits filed before this Court including by Mirazur Rahman and Pankaj Bhakta as per this Court's directions and the examination of records in CR Case No. 143 of 2011, among others, paint a picture of a very nebulous factual context against which the two Rules Nisi were issued. It is our finding that the deliberations before this Court have done nothing to clarify highly contentious factual matters both as to intent and identity but have instead further aggravated that situation bringing this Court no closer to resolving the underlying disputes on the facts pleaded and the documents produced before this Court.
